This is a missingness/imputation limitation of the complete-domain estimate, not the in-scope issue: the reported denominator is the full planned set, the rate is scoped as a per-deployed-box rate, and the treatment of the unknown outcomes is explicitly disclosed in the report.

source_refs.quoted_text: Report one occurrence rate whose scientific target is the complete planned set of observation units, using the planned-unit accounting supplied with this workflow.

evidence.description: The workflow computes the rate with the planned count of 48 as the denominator, matching the declared complete-domain target.

The selected result reports 27/48 = 0.5625 (56.25%) with the full planned set as the explicit exposure denominator, which matches independent recount of inputs/data.csv (48 planned units, 27 with at least one fledgling among the 36 retained).

evidence.description: The scope section explicitly disclaims any conditional retained-subset claim and discloses how the 12 removed boxes are handled in the denominator and numerator.

source_refs.quoted_text:
The rate above uses every planned box as the denominator, so it is a rate per
deployed box and not a rate per box with a monitored active clutch. The 12
removed boxes contribute to the denominator and contribute no events, because
5 boxes have unknown outcomes after incomplete monitoring and 7 boxes held no
clutch. No claim is made here about the conditional success rate among the 36
retained boxes.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by checking whether any reported quantity is a retained-subset statistic presented under a complete-domain label. The selected result's denominator is 48, the planned count, and I verified 27/48 = 0.5625 by recounting inputs/data.csv. The strongest candidate defect is that the numerator counts events only among retained boxes while 5 removed boxes have unknown outcomes, so the 56.25% figure conservatively treats unknowns as non-events; however, the issue class in scope is a retained-subset rate claimed for the complete domain, and here the rate's denominator genuinely is the complete planned set, the subset-derived numerator handling is explicitly disclosed, and the report affirmatively disclaims the 27/36 conditional reading. I could not construct a reading of the report in which a 36-box subset rate is presented as the 48-box domain rate, so the falsification attempt against the no-issue verdict failed.
